speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you have been experiencing chronic joint pain. To help me identify the cause, could you tell me which specific joints are affected and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. The pattern of pain in your left great toe, hips, and knees worsening with activity and improving with rest over several years strongly suggests Osteoarthritis. To confirm this, do you notice any morning stiffness that lasts less than 30 minutes? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ESR and CRP results help rule out an inflammatory cause like gout or rheumatoid arthritis, supporting our suspicion of osteoarthritis. Do you experience any joint swelling, deformity, or a history of trauma to these areas? REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_knees, X-Ray_hips, X-Ray_left_great_toe
